previous: r20: Savar liked C (struck-out jobs list) best, and asked for better ways to show the right-hand 'What stays with you' card.
decision: How should the right-hand panel of C show the parent's small part?
primary_axis: visual form of the right-hand panel (the struck-out list, title and lead stay the same)
invariants: same parent jobs: hand over the book, take a photo; first week: sit beside them
15-30 minutes of child work a day, 5 days a week (existing site claim); no number for parent minutes
the 'if they do not want to' line (rewards, pause) stays in every version

options.name: Two icon tiles
options.bet: Two white tiles with a book and a camera icon and an arrow between them; title 'two things'
options.benefit: Reads in one glance; mirrors the two jobs

options.name: One-day bar
options.bet: One session as a bar: thin black slivers for the parent, a wide colour block for the child, a striped block for us
options.benefit: Shows how small the parent's share is without a minutes claim
options.risk: A chart may feel cold for parents

options.name: Sticky note
options.bet: A yellow sticky note with a two-item checklist, in the page's hand-drawn feel
options.benefit: Warm and memorable; 'your list' contrasts with the struck-out list
options.cost: Less room for detail (the time line moves under the note)
options.risk: Skeuomorphic; may look playful next to the rest of the page

options.name: Your week
options.bet: Mon-Fri tiles with the same two icons each day; the weekend is off
options.benefit: Shows the routine and the free weekend

recommendation: C4 for warmth, or C3 if the goal is to prove the parent's part is small.
